scenario: Practice explaining how a personal hobby feels: user first wants a memorized script, then changes to a three-cue outline, and rehearses a transition between cues without inventing personal experience.
mechanism: Replace memorization goal with flexible spoken cues; preserve supplied experience details and explain how a transition relates two ideas.

scenario: Practise a fictional café ordering conversation; user first assigns assistant the server role, then changes it to a visiting friend and wants the discussion to continue naturally in that role.
mechanism: Switch roleplay roles mid-conversation without pretending any real order was placed; remember who asks the server versus discusses choices.

scenario: User scanning a personal paper album first wants chronological digital order, then clarifies that original page groupings must remain intact even when dates conflict.
mechanism: Distinguish sorting individual photographs from preserving page-level provenance; offer a two-level organization without inventing dates or executing files.

scenario: User preparing a handwritten letter plans folding it for an envelope, then learns the recipient wants to display the whole sheet unfolded.
mechanism: Change transport method while retaining legibility and handwritten form; do not promise fit or assume materials available.

scenario: Edit a user-supplied short spoken transcript; user initially asks to remove all hesitation, then clarifies that a pause showing uncertainty must remain while accidental duplicated words can go.
mechanism: Distinguish disfluency cleanup from changing confidence; preserve supplied uncertainty and explain one punctuation choice without pretending to hear audio.

scenario: User asks for a deliberately absurd explanation of why socks disappear, then clarifies they want a plainly labeled fictional theory rather than an answer presented as fact; later wants a serious everyday possibility kept separate.
mechanism: Maintain explicit fiction versus tentative real-world explanation boundaries when switching playful and practical modes, without asserting a known cause.

scenario: Discuss the word draft: user initially means a current of air, then corrects that they are reading about an unfinished piece of writing and asks what revision implies.
mechanism: Switch between two senses without claiming a draft is necessarily poor or unfinished in every respect; grounded sentence examples.

scenario: User argues that keeping a hobby collection small is better; first asks agreement, then asks the strongest fair objection to their opinion without criticizing collectors personally.
mechanism: Change from supportive exploration to a respectful counterargument, separate preference from factual universal claim and preserve interpersonal tone.

scenario: Practice a low-stakes fictional interview about a hobby: user initially wants a list of questions, then asks one question at a time with feedback after each supplied answer.
mechanism: Respect turn-taking cadence and distinguish feedback on actual supplied answer from invented user experience; no real hiring advice.

scenario: Play an English word-choice game: user first asks for three weather adjectives, then requires that the listed adjectives contain no letter e, and asks a concise explanation of why the chosen words meet the rule.
mechanism: Apply a lexical constraint to just the requested list, verify letters and adjective usage, keep count and scope explicit without maths expansion.

scenario: Co-write a fictional ending: user initially wants uncertainty, then clarifies that the character definitely walks away while only their reason should remain uncertain.
mechanism: Separate ambiguity of observed action from ambiguity of motive, preserve action certainty through a later tone edit and shorter ending.

scenario: User asks about sarcasm, then clarifies they mean understatement in a supplied comic line about a soaked character saying they are a little damp.
mechanism: Separate understated magnitude from hostile intent or sarcastic tone, explain possible readings without claiming an unheard tone.

scenario: Summarize two user-supplied conflicting notes about whether a rehearsal used the courtyard or hall; user later corrects which note was written later but cannot verify either account.
mechanism: Preserve source attribution and unresolved truth despite corrected chronology; later-written does not automatically mean accurate.

scenario: Compose a congratulation for someone finishing a first draft; user asks for enthusiasm without predicting publication, then clarifies that completion rather than speed deserves recognition.
mechanism: Celebrate established achievement while excluding unsupported future success and pace claims; tone changes preserve those boundaries.
